productIntroInfra: We added safe USDC helpers for Arc — they avoid decimal and gas footguns — plus this test playground.
productIntroAudience: This is only a visual sample for product teams.
productIntroRepoLead: Developers go straight to the code here:
heroLede: Three product lessons: why other chains show two balances, why an Ethereum template can accept an incomplete payment, and why gas on Arc reads in dollars. One USDC. No wallet yet — that ships next.
convLede: Problem: on Ethereum and in many templates the wallet shows two balances (native + USDC). It looks like double money — or it’s unclear how much you have. Arc improvement: USDC is native — gas and balance are in dollars. Show one row; don’t duplicate the money on screen.
convArcDocsBlurb: On Arc, USDC is the native gas and balance unit — your UI should show one dollar balance, not native plus ERC-20 rows.
amountHint: Try “50” (salary) or “12.50” (invoice). One digital dollar = 1 USDC.
amountError: Enter a valid amount, for example 50 or 12.50 (up to 6 decimals).
balanceOneRow: One USDC row — the same money, not duplicated on screen.
techDetailsBody: Under the hood Arc represents the same amount with two precision scales; the UI should still show a single USDC:
naiveLedeAmount: Problem: you collect {amount}. An Ethereum template often uses the wrong decimal scale and thinks a tiny fraction is enough — it accepts the payment and you come up short. Arc improvement: compare the full USDC amount before saying OK; the incomplete payment is rejected.
naiveLedeFallback: Problem: an Ethereum template often uses the wrong decimal scale and thinks a tiny fraction is enough — it accepts the payment and you come up short. Arc improvement: compare the full USDC amount before saying OK; the incomplete payment is rejected.
naiveArcDocsBlurb: When you connect a wallet or backend to Arc, payment checks must use the chain’s USDC precision — not an Ethereum mainnet mental model.
naiveEthAccepts: Accepts the payment — you come up short!
naiveArcBody: Compares the full USDC value before saying OK.
naiveArcDidNotReject: Did not reject the incomplete amount
naiveFixAmount: Fix the amount above to see the comparison.
naiveDustHint: That’s why one well-rounded dollar balance matters: on-chain “dust” can look like $0.00 USDC on screen and still exist on-chain.
feeTitle: 3. You send a payment: how much gas in dollars?
feeLede: Problem: on other chains gas is paid in an unfamiliar token (ETH, etc.) so the cost doesn’t read in dollars; and if the price sits under the minimum, the transaction can vanish. Arc improvement: gas is paid in USDC — you see a predictable dollar cost. Meet the 20 Gwei minimum or the transaction may never confirm.
feeArcDocsBlurb: Arc charges gas in USDC with a network minimum fee per gas — below the floor, transactions may not confirm.
feeFloorHint: Arc minimum: {floor} Gwei. The cost is shown in USDC (dollars).
feeBelowFloor: The price is under the 20 Gwei minimum: on Arc this transaction may never confirm and leave no trace.
feeOkFloor: Meets the minimum: the cost is charged in USDC and the transaction can land.
